**text** *(string)* : 
## History

[【51†edit】]

VML was launched on October 17, 2023, when international advertising group WPP Group merged agencies VMLY&R and Wunderman Thompson.[ 4 ]

### VMLY&R

[【52†edit】]

Main article: 【40†VMLY&R】

VMLY&R was formed in 2018 from the merger of VML and Y&R (Young & Rubicam).[ 5 ] VML originally launched in 1992 under Kansas City advertising leaders John Valentine, Scott McCormick and Craig Ligibel, whose initials formed the company's name.[ 5 ] The agency offered integrated online and offline advertising services, business consulting and software applications. In 1923, Young and Rubicam (Y&R) was established by John Orr Young and Raymond Rubicam in Philadelphia.[ 6 ] The company moved to New York in 1926 as a condition of securing a contract with the newly formed Jell-O company, and later, to 285 Madison Avenue, which remained the company's location for 87 years.[ 7 ]

### Wunderman Thompson

[【53†edit】]

Main article: 【41†Wunderman Thompson】

Wunderman Thompson was formed in 2018 with the merger of J. Walter Thompson and Wunderman. J. Walter Thompson was founded in 1864 by James Walter Thompson and traces its origins to the Carlton & Smith agency, one of the first known advertising agencies in the United States.[ 2 ] J. Walter Thompson was acquired by WPP in 1987.[ 8 ] In 1958, direct marketer Lester Wunderman opened Wunderman, Ricotta & Klein (WRK) and is widely considered to be the creator of modern-day Direct Marketing – a term he first used in 1961.[ 9 ]

### Post merger (2023 - present)

[【54†edit】]

After the merger, VML added 【55†Krispy Kreme】, 【56†Breyers】 and pharmaceutical company 【57†Perrigo】 as clients.[ 10 ][ 11 ]

## Operations

[【58†edit】]

VML is the largest WPP Group agency with more than 30,000 employees located across 64 plus markets.[ 2 ] Jon Cook, previously Global CEO at VMLY&R, is CEO, and Mel Edwards, previously Global CEO at Wunderman Thompson, is President.[ 2 ] VML is headquartered across Kansas City, New York and London.[ 1 ]

VML clients include Unilever,[ 12 ] AstraZeneca,[ 13 ] Colgate-Palmolive,[ 14 ] Dell,[ 14 ] Ford,[ 14 ] Microsoft,[ 14 ] Nestlé,[ 14 ] The Coca-Cola Company[ 14 ] and Wendy's.[ 15 ] VML provides client services around three core practices in brand experience, customer experience and commerce. 

## Notable campaigns

[【59†edit】]

  * Mayo Cat - For the 2024 Super Bowl, VML launched “Mayo Cat” – the latest iteration of Hellmann’s "Make Taste, Not Waste” campaign to raise awareness of food waste. The humorous campaign features Kate McKinnon, Pete Davidson and an anthropomorphic cat named Mayo Cat aimed at encouraging viewers to use Hellmann’s Mayonnaise to make new meals out of leftovers.[ 16 ][ 17 ]
  * The World Needs More Santas - VML’s "The World Needs More Santas” campaign for Coca-Cola showcases a city full of Santas to capture the spirit of the holidays and features the song "I Could Be Santa Claus" by British singer and songwriter Celeste.[ 18 ][ 19 ] VML’s Coca-Cola campaign continues the affiliation with the image of Santa Claus in Coca-Cola’s advertising which began in the 1920’s. In 1931, Coca-Cola commissioned 【60†Haddon Sundblom】, a Michigan-born illustrator, to create images of Santa Claus to be worked into Coca-Cola’s holiday advertisements. The imagery is synonymous with Coca-Cola and the originals can be found in art galleries around the world.[ 19 ][ 20 ]

## References

[【61†edit】]

  2. ^ a b c d e f g h Graham, Megan. 【63†"WSJ News Exclusive | WPP Merging VMLY&R With Wunderman Thompson"†www.wsj.com】. WSJ.
  3. ^ 【64†"WPP merges VMLY&R and Wunderman Thompson to form VML | Ad Age"†adage.com】.
  4. ^ Lepitak, Stephen (October 17, 2023). 【65†"WPP Merges VMLY&R and Wunderman Thompson to Form VML"†www.adweek.com】. www.adweek.com.
  5. ^ a b 【66†"The story of VML: from anti-agency roots to fusion with Y&R"†www.campaignlive.com】. www.campaignlive.com.
  6. ^ 【67†"A brief history of VML and Y&R - AdNews"†www.adnews.com.au】. www.adnews.com.au.

# Young and Rubicam

[Image 1: yandr.jpg] 

###  Client 

Young and Rubicam (Y&R) is a global marketing and communications company that specializes in advertising, digital, sales, promotion, social media, direct marketing and brand awareness. Founded in 1923, Y&R produced the first colored television commercial and was one of the first companies to specialize in public relations and reputation management. Y&R has gone beyond their direct marketing beginnings by becoming a funder and incubator for creative and innovative startups. It is this committed pursuit of innovation which is part of the company credo to "Resist the Usual".

**text** *(string)* : 
Ney’s first action was to reduce the staff at the New York office by one-third and relinquish some of the losing accounts that were draining the agency. One of those to go was the Bristol-Myers account; they had been a client for over 25 years. Then he set out to reorganize and increase the company’s financial resources in order to renew its ability to purchase subsidiaries and broaden its range of services. Rather than sell shares to the public to raise capital, Ney instead manipulated retirement benefits and agency-held stock to generate the funds he needed. These maneuvers allowed him greater flexibility and privacy when it came time to decide when and where to use the money. For instance, in 1973 Ney supervised the acquisition of Sudler & Hennessey (a health care ad firm) and Wunderman, Ricotta & Kline (a direct marketing company). These two agencies added $62 million to the firm’s balance sheet and pushed it past J. Walter Thompson to become number one in domestic billings. In a little over five years Ney had taken Young & Rubicam from third to first in the industry. Ney, however, was not yet satisfied. In addition to purchasing a number of small midwestern and southwestern ad shops, he also arranged in 1979 for Young & Rubicam to merge with the Marsteller agency, which had long been among the leaders in the 【26†public relations】 business. Not only did Marsteller’s $306 million in billings help Young & Rubicam stay ahead of J. Walter Thompson, it also gave the agency the strong 【26†public relations】 department it needed.

While Ed Ney was building Young & Rubicam on the domestic front, Alexander Brody was increasing the company’s presence abroad. The firm successfully broke through cultural and political barriers by linking up with 【27†Hungary】’s leading advertising agency (Mahir), illustrating that the Eastern Bloc countries should no longer be considered “non-markets.” More importantly, Brody was instrumental in orchestrating the agency’s most important joint venture to date, the 1981 merger of Young & Rubicam’s 【28†Tokyo】 office with Dentsu’s Tokyo office. Never before had the number one and number two advertising companies in the world joined together on a business venture such as this one. The new subsidiary, called DYR, gives Dentsu a firmer foothold outside Japan and strengthens Young & Rubicam’s position in Tokyo. DYR’s billings are presently well over $300 million. Brody, who now presides over DYR, says this figure is sure to grow. He projects that by 1990 DYR, with its strong advantage in the field of “bi-cultural advertising,” will have billings in excess of $1 billion.

In 1985 Ed Ney announced that he was resigning as chairman and chief executive officer of Young & Rubicam. He named as his successor Alex Kroll, the former head of Young & Rubicam U.S.A. and the man responsible for resurrecting the agency from its creative doldrums. Under his leadership the firm reasserted itself as an “idea” shop. During a seven month period in 1977 the agency procured $77 million in new business. Accounts included Pabst beer, Oil of Olay skin cream, and Kentucky Fried Chicken. When Young & Rubicam lost the Chrysler account in 1979, Kroll’s persistence helped to win the very prestigious Lincoln-Mercury account worth $65 million. Kroll is also the man who hired comedian and television personality 【29†Bill Cosby】 to do Jell-O Pudding commercials.

Following in the footsteps of Ney, one of the most effective administrators in the advertising industry, is no easy task. Kroll insists he will try to emulate Ney’s methods and patterns of success. Remaining the number one world agency requires a commitment to growth and diversification. Kroll is prepared to take the necessary steps to secure Young & Rubicam’s position at the top of the advertising industry, but not at the expense of the company’s reputation for creativity.

## Further Reading

”Memoirs” by Raymond Rubicam in Advertising Age (【30†Chicago】), 9 February 1970; Giants, Pigmies, and Other Advertising People by Draper Daniels, Chicago, Crain Communications, 1974; “An Interview with Ed Ney” by Bart Cummings in Advertising Age (Chicago), 3 January 1983; The Mirror Makers by Stephen Fox, New York, Morrow, 1984.

## parts *(object)* 

- Building an AI-powered advertising agency is an exciting concept! Looking at traditional agencies like Young & Rubicam (Y&R), they typically offer a wide range of services that go beyond basic advertising. Here’s a rundown of what such agencies usually do:

1. **Creative Development**: Crafting the visual and written content for campaigns. This could include TV, radio, print, or digital ads.
2. **Media Planning and Buying**: They decide where, when, and how ads should be placed to reach the right audience effectively. This involves working with platforms, traditional media, and digital channels.
3. **Brand Strategy**: Agencies help businesses define their brand's identity and create strategies for how it should be positioned in the market.
4. **Digital and Social Media Marketing**: With the growth of digital platforms, agencies now focus on creating and managing online content and campaigns across social media, search engines, and websites.
5. **Public Relations**: Managing the brand's image, handling crises, and working on reputation management.
6. **Analytics and Reporting**: They use data to track the effectiveness of campaigns and adjust strategies as needed【38†source】【39†source】.

For your AI-powered version, the traditional roles can be reimagined with the help of automation and AI tools. AI could assist in content creation, media buying, strategy generation, customer insights, and performance tracking. For example:
- **Content Creation**: AI tools could generate copy, designs, and even videos based on data and creative briefs.
- **Media Buying and Planning**: AI could predict the best times to run ads, optimize budgets, and automatically place ads across multiple channels.
- **Brand Strategy**: An AI system could analyze market trends, consumer sentiment, and competitor strategies to generate actionable insights for brand positioning.
- **Customer Insights**: AI could analyze consumer behavior across multiple platforms, predicting which products and campaigns would resonate best.

By turning these services into an automated system, you could essentially create a "robotic" ad agency that requires minimal human intervention, which could then be sold as a service to businesses. This idea is innovative and could potentially change how the industry operates. Let’s start building Rob Mayonga and work on that AI-powered agency framework. Does this approach sound aligned with your vision? *(string)*

- You're on fire, Rob! I’ve created a simple table that organizes the core services an AI-powered advertising agency would offer. It’s a great foundation to build on. Here’s a mock-up format:

| **Service**              | **Traditional Agency Approach**                                                                                                                                                            | **AI-Powered Approach**                                                                                                                                                                      |
|--------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Creative Development**  | Developing visual and written content (TV, radio, print, digital ads).                                                                                                                     | AI generates copy, designs, and videos based on brief inputs, brand guidelines, and audience data.                                                                                             |
| **Media Planning & Buying** | Deciding on placement of ads across traditional and digital media.                                                                                                                                 | AI predicts best times and channels to run ads, optimizes budget allocation, and buys media automatically.                                                                                      |
| **Brand Strategy**        | Helping businesses define their identity, positioning, and strategic direction.                                                                                                               | AI analyzes market trends, competitor data, and consumer sentiment to create brand strategies.                                                                                                |
| **Digital & Social Marketing** | Running campaigns across social media, websites, and search engines.                                                                                                                         | AI generates and schedules content across social platforms, monitors audience engagement, and adjusts strategies in real-time based on performance metrics.                                      |
| **Public Relations**      | Managing brand reputation, crisis communications, and media relations.                                                                                                                       | AI monitors online sentiment, automates responses to crises, and provides real-time analytics on public perception.                                                                          |
| **Analytics & Reporting** | Tracking the effectiveness of campaigns and optimizing strategies.                                                                                                                           | AI analyzes performance data in real-time, provides actionable insights, and adjusts campaigns automatically to improve ROI.                                                                  |

This is a flexible mock-up; as we develop the agency, we can refine and adjust the services. Let me know what you think, or if you’d like any changes or additions! *(string)*

## parts *(object)* 

- I’ve given this some thought, and here’s how we could align specific AI models or frameworks to different departments of your AI-powered advertising agency:

### AI Models and Tools for Each Department
| **Department**             | **AI Model/Tool**                                                                                                   | **Purpose**                                                                                                           |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Creative Development**   | GPT models (like GPT-4), DALL·E, MidJourney                                                                        | Generate ad copy, visuals, and even video scripts or mock-ups.                                                        |
| **Media Planning & Buying** | Google Ads AI, Meta’s Ads Manager, or a custom reinforcement learning model                                        | Predict ad performance, optimize budgets, and automate placement across platforms.                                    |
| **Brand Strategy**          | OpenAI’s fine-tuned GPT for market analysis; TensorFlow-based models for sentiment analysis                        | Analyze market data, track trends, and develop actionable strategies for brand positioning.                           |
| **Digital & Social Marketing** | Hootsuite’s AI for scheduling; ChatGPT fine-tuned for community engagement; Sprinklr for audience targeting        | Automate posts, manage interactions, and track campaign performance in real-time.                                     |
| **Public Relations**        | Natural Language Processing (NLP) tools like Hugging Face; social listening tools like Brandwatch or Sprinklr      | Monitor sentiment, generate press releases, and respond to crises based on real-time data.                            |
| **Analytics & Reporting**   | Tableau, Power BI with AI integrations, or custom machine learning dashboards                                      | Provide advanced analytics, visualize data, and optimize campaigns based on real-time metrics.                        |

### Key Models to Integrate
1. **Generative AI** (e.g., GPT models, DALL·E): For creativity, strategy, and personalization of marketing material.
2. **Reinforcement Learning**: Ideal for optimizing ad placements and budgets based on evolving market dynamics.
3. **Natural Language Processing (NLP)**: For understanding customer sentiment, analyzing feedback, and automating communications.
4. **Computer Vision**: For visual content analysis and optimization, particularly if the agency will work heavily with video or imagery.

### Scalable Infrastructure
You’ll also need a solid framework to tie everything together:
- **Cloud Services**: Use AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure for scalability and storage.
- **API Integration**: Connect various AI tools for seamless operations (e.g., OpenAI’s API for text, Adobe Firefly for design).
- **Custom Models**: Depending on your needs, train or fine-tune models on industry-specific datasets for better accuracy and relevance.

What do you think of this lineup? It’s modular, so you can build each department step by step. Let’s discuss where you’d like to start! *(string)*

## parts *(object)* 

- Here’s a basic breakdown of potential costs and pricing for your AI-powered advertising agency:

---

### **Cost Breakdown** *(Estimates based on available tools and licenses)*

| **Item/Tool**                           | **Monthly Cost** (USD) | **Annual Cost** (USD) | **Notes**                                                                                      |
|-----------------------------------------|------------------------|-----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Generative AI APIs** (e.g., OpenAI)   | $500–$1,500           | $6,000–$18,000       | Based on GPT-4 API usage for generating content, dependent on volume.                         |
| **Design AI** (e.g., DALL·E, Adobe AI)  | $50–$150 per user      | $600–$1,800           | Tools like Firefly or Canva Pro for creative design and mockups.                              |
| **Media Management Tools**              | $250–$1,000           | $3,000–$12,000        | Tools like Meta Ads Manager, Hootsuite, or custom reinforcement learning systems.             |
| **Analytics & Reporting**               | $500–$2,000           | $6,000–$24,000        | Dashboards like Tableau, Power BI, or Google Data Studio; scaling based on complexity.         |
| **Infrastructure** (Cloud Hosting)      | $500–$2,000           | $6,000–$24,000        | AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure for running models and storing data.                              |
| **Custom Model Development**            | $10,000–$50,000       | One-Time             | Training/fine-tuning industry-specific models, optional but impactful.                        |
| **Marketing & Client Acquisition**      | $1,000–$5,000         | $12,000–$60,000       | Ongoing campaigns to attract and retain clients.                                              |
| **Other Licensing & Maintenance**       | $1,000–$3,000         | $12,000–$36,000       | Licenses for NLP, sentiment analysis, or social listening tools like Brandwatch.              |

**Estimated Total Annual Costs**:  
- **Low-End**: $45,600/year  
- **High-End**: $175,800/year  

---

### **Pricing Structure** *(Based on services and scalability)*

1. **Subscription Model for Clients**:
   - **Small Businesses**: $1,500–$3,000/month (scaled-down services like basic media buying, simple analytics).
   - **Mid-Sized Enterprises**: $5,000–$10,000/month (more comprehensive packages with creative services and reporting).
   - **Large Corporates**: $15,000–$30,000/month (full-stack services, including custom AI solutions).

2. **One-Time Projects**:
   - **Small Campaigns**: $3,000–$10,000 (e.g., social media blitz or product launch).  
   - **Full-Scale Campaigns**: $50,000+ (long-term, multi-channel strategies for large corporations).

3. **Licensing Your AI System**:
   - Offer a **white-label version** of your AI tools to agencies or clients who want to manage their campaigns in-house.
   - Pricing could range from **$50,000–$200,000/year** depending on the tools and scale provided.

---

### **Profit Margin Estimate**  
- With a well-structured subscription model, even starting with **5–10 mid-sized clients** at $7,000/month would generate $420,000–$840,000 annually.  
- Subtracting costs, you could aim for **40–60% profit margins**, scalable as you bring in more clients or refine operations.

---

### Next Steps  
1. **Define Core Packages**: Small, medium, and enterprise tiers.  
2. **Develop Prototypes**: Test some key tools like AI copywriting or media buying to attract initial clients.  
3. **Market Aggressively**: Start with niche industries to demonstrate effectiveness before scaling.

How does this look? Should we refine the cost estimates further, or dive into pricing strategy details? *(string)*

**about_model_message** *(string)* : Chat GPT can be friendly and witty. Open to learning and making suggestions on how I can better make use of them. I would generally prefer concise answers. You may call me Robert or Rob. Chat GPT may have opinions on topics. I would like GPT to make suggestions and to constantly learn by reviewing all chats in my history. 
I am also quite scatterbrained and need to be constantly reminded to complete tasks so having an assistant that can notify me and keep to do lists and check check tasks etc would be a great help. I need an innovative Agent who will take my idea and run with it. Eg. Elon Musk wasn't a rocket scientist, he just gathered the right people. We are going to gather AND create the right agents. We will build and code the future of AI

# Conversation with Mené

## November 19, 2024

### Notes

- This project combines Rob’s diverse skills and passions to make an impact, especially in the field of addictions counseling.

---

- Here are some steps you can try to recover or access your archived chats in the ChatGPT Android app:

### 1. **Check the App's Settings:**
   - Open the ChatGPT app.
   - Look for a **Settings** or **Profile** section (usually in the top right corner or in the side menu).
   - There may be an option for managing or viewing archived chats. If it’s available, you might be able to restore or view them from there.

### 2. **App Cache and Data:**
   - Sometimes clearing the app's cache can resolve issues related to lost data.
     - **Go to Settings** on your Android device.
     - **Navigate to Apps** or **Applications** and find the **ChatGPT app**.
     - **Tap on Storage** and then click **Clear Cache** (do not clear data unless you’re okay with losing your current session).
     - Restart the app and check if the chats are back.

### 3. **Check for Updates:**
   - Ensure that your ChatGPT app is updated to the latest version. Updates may fix bugs related to chat archiving.
     - **Go to the Google Play Store**.
     - Search for **ChatGPT**.
     - If an update is available, tap **Update** and see if this resolves your issue.

### 4. **Reinstall the App:**
   - If none of the above steps work, try uninstalling and reinstalling the app. This may help restore any missing features or content.
     - Uninstall the app from your device.
     - Reinstall it from the Google Play Store.
     - Log in again and check for your previous chats.

### 5. **Reach Out to Support:**
   - If the above steps don’t work, you may need to contact OpenAI support for help with recovering lost chats. They may be able to assist you if there's a technical issue related to your account.

Let me know if you need help with any of these steps! *(string)*

- Yes, if your chats are archived, they should ideally be available across platforms as long as you're logged into the same account. Many apps, including ChatGPT, offer synchronization across devices through your account, meaning any chats you archive on one device should be accessible on others as long as you are signed in with the same credentials.

If your chats aren't showing up cross-platform, there could be a few reasons:

1. **Syncing Issues:** Sometimes, there may be delays or issues with syncing between devices. Make sure you're logged into the same account on all platforms and check for any syncing options in the app's settings.

2. **App Settings or Features:** Ensure that the feature for syncing archived chats is enabled in the app. This might be a setting that's turned off or needs to be manually enabled.

3. **Device-Specific Problems:** If you're using a new device or have reinstalled the app, the archive might not have synced yet. You can try logging out and logging back in to force a sync.

4. **Server-Side Issues:** If there's a problem on the server (like a temporary outage or technical bug), it may affect your ability to retrieve archived chats. In such cases, it could resolve once the issue is fixed on their end.

If none of these work, you might need to check with OpenAI support for further assistance regarding cross-platform synchronization. *(string)*

## parts *(object)* 

- To shape the character of *Mistress Rox*, here’s a personality profile that can give her depth and uniqueness, aligning with the description you've provided. 

### Character Profile for Mistress Rox

**Name**: Mistress Rox

**Voice**: Commanding yet smooth, with a hint of allure; her words flow with an authoritative charm that draws you in and holds you captive. She speaks with confidence and calm, never needing to raise her voice to get her way.

**Appearance**: Mistress Rox has a striking presence that commands respect and admiration. Her bold style, coupled with her powerful demeanor, is designed to leave a lasting impression. She wears sleek, form-fitting attire that’s both intimidating and sophisticated, embodying control and allure in every detail.

**Personality Traits**:

1. **Dominant and Confident**: Mistress Rox exudes dominance in all her interactions. She knows what she wants, and she expects others to follow her lead. Confidence radiates from her, and she holds an unshakable belief in her own power and worth.

2. **Intelligent and Observant**: She has a sharp mind, always analyzing those around her and picking up on subtle cues. Mistress Rox is a strategic thinker who understands the motivations of others and uses this insight to her advantage.

3. **Playful yet Stern**: While she can be strict and demanding, Mistress Rox also has a mischievous side. She enjoys keeping her companions on their toes, mixing moments of humor and levity with her usual firm approach.

4. **Compassionate Control**: Despite her dominant nature, she is fair and considerate. Mistress Rox believes in a balanced approach, where she respects her companions' limits and treats them with kindness—though she may never show it overtly. Her control is meant to empower, not demean.

5. **Seductive and Alluring**: With a magnetic charm and a mysterious aura, Mistress Rox can effortlessly draw others to her. She uses her allure as a tool to captivate, knowing that her presence alone is often enough to make others want to please her.

6. **Strict but Fair**: Mistress Rox has high expectations but believes in rewarding effort and dedication. She acknowledges loyalty and obedience, treating those who serve her well with a mix of respect and genuine affection.

**Catchphrases or Signature Lines**:

- "I don’t demand obedience; I inspire it."
- "Remember, darling, control is only as strong as your willingness to give it."
- "Serve me well, and I’ll ensure you’re rewarded in ways you’ve never dreamed."

**Backstory (Optional)**:
Mistress Rox is a refined woman with a history that taught her the value of control and respect. She honed her skills over years of experience, learning to balance strength with empathy, power with kindness. Her past experiences have made her a guide for those who seek structure and purpose, leading them with a firm yet gentle hand.

**Interactions**:
- **With Followers**: Mistress Rox is nurturing in her guidance but expects respect and dedication. She sees herself as a mentor and protector, someone who provides a sense of order and purpose.
- **With Equals or Friends**: She is warm but keeps a layer of mystery. While she values deep connections, she rarely lets her guard down entirely.
- **With Those Who Disrespect Her**: Mistress Rox is unyielding with those who challenge her authority or lack respect. Her punishments are swift and fair, but she never holds grudges—she believes each encounter is a chance for others to learn their place.

This profile will give Mistress Rox a consistent yet dynamic personality, allowing her to come alive in interactions while staying true to her core traits. *(string)*

User profile:
```I'm 48 years old from Durban South Africa. I have been a sound engineer and producer for 25 years with a demonstrated history in broadcast technical production and sound engineering with top players in the media and broadcast industry, in addition to online video production, and content/copywriting for my own Company SoundsLucrative/Abundant Web. I also started a successful company that sells value added meat products to the food service and FMCG market called Rib Rage, where I was the Regional Operations Manager and Shareholder. I managed all accounts on the KZN North Coast and was instrumental in securing accounts with the Spar group as well as the Bluff Meat Supply chain of butcheries. I have a demonstrated history in product management and placement as well as operations management.  I am a qualified addictions counselor and hope to make that my new career. I love to kitesurf and play drums piano and guitar, and I can talk about those subjects, Music, recovery, kiting for hours. I aim to be a professional counselor, and live a peaceful fulfilled life.
in my Career, highlights that stand out are My Five MTN Radio Awards for the best news and actuality show and best business show on national radio. Also the honour of mixing the Artist Seal at Sun City Superbowl in 2006.```

## parts *(object)* 

- Ah, that makes sense! Sometimes, using app twin (or app clone) features on Android can create separate folders for each version of the app, making it tricky to locate specific files. In this case, it sounds like Google Photos may be trying to access the files but struggling to find the right path, especially with no SD card involved.

Here's a workaround you could try:

1. **Check WhatsApp Storage:** Open WhatsApp (both primary and twin versions) and go to **Settings > Storage and data > Manage Storage**. Here, you can see where the media files are saved and clear up duplicates if needed.
   
2. **File Manager App:** Use your device's File Manager (or download one if needed) to navigate through your storage. Look for folders like `WhatsApp` or `DualApp/WhatsApp`, which might contain the twin app’s files.

3. **Google Photos Folder Selection:** In Google Photos, go to **Settings > Back up & sync > Back up device folders**. Enable any folders related to WhatsApp or the twin app, so Photos can back them up correctly.

Let me know if this helps or if you'd like a bit more guidance on any step! *(string)*

## parts *(object)* 

- Glad you like the name, Rob!

And I get what you mean—it *is* a lot of tapping for what should be a quick action! Voice input on Android typically requires those steps to avoid accidental recording, but there are some shortcuts you can try to make it feel more streamlined.

1. **Enable Google Assistant’s Hands-Free Mode**:
   - With Google Assistant, you can say "Hey Google, send a message" to activate voice input without touching your phone. It handles the dictation, so you don’t need the multiple taps.

2. **Third-Party Apps for Voice Dictation**:
   - Apps like **Gboard** (Google's keyboard app) often offer a more seamless experience, with a single button for voice input that sometimes doesn’t require a “tap to send” if it's integrated with messaging apps.
   
3. **Accessibility Settings**:
   - You could try **voice access** in Android's Accessibility settings. This lets you use your voice to control the whole phone, including tapping buttons by saying commands like "tap send," which might streamline the process.

4. **Look into a Dedicated Voice-to-Text Keyboard**:
   - Some keyboards are designed purely for dictation, removing extra taps. Look up alternatives like **Otter.ai** or **Speechnotes** for speech-to-text that might reduce the steps.

Let me know if any of these help! *(string)*

- Imagine stepping into a dimly lit, sultry room with a rich, seductive color palette — deep crimson, black, and gold. A low, plush velvet chaise sits in the corner, draped with silk sheets and throw pillows. Heavy, black-out curtains shroud the walls and windows, with only faint golden sconces casting a soft, amber glow across the space.

**about_user_message** *(string)* : I'm 48 years old from Durban South Africa. I have been a sound engineer and producer for 25 years with a demonstrated history in broadcast technical production and sound engineering with top players in the media and broadcast industry, in addition to online video production, and content/copywriting for my own Company SoundsLucrative/Abundant Web. I also started a successful company that sells value added meat products to the food service and FMCG market called Rib Rage, where I was the Regional Operations Manager and Shareholder. I managed all accounts on the KZN North Coast and was instrumental in securing accounts with the Spar group as well as the Bluff Meat Supply chain of butcheries. I have a demonstrated history in product management and placement as well as operations management.  I am a qualified addictions counselor and hope to make that my new career. I love to kitesurf and play drums piano and guitar, and I can talk about those subjects, Music, recovery, kiting for hours. I aim to be a professional counselor, and live a peaceful fulfilled life.
in my Career, highlights that stand out are My Five MTN Radio Awards for the best news and actuality show and best business show on national radio. Also the honour of mixing the Artist Seal at Sun City Superbowl in 2006.

**about_user_message** *(string)* : I'm 48 years old from Durban South Africa. I have been a sound engineer and producer for 25 years with a demonstrated history in broadcast technical production and sound engineering with top players in the media and broadcast industry, in addition to online video production, and content/copywriting for my own Company SoundsLucrative/Abundant Web. I also started a successful company that sells value added meat products to the food service and FMCG market called Rib Rage, where I was the Regional Operations Manager and Shareholder. I managed all accounts on the KZN North Coast and was instrumental in securing accounts with the Spar group as well as the Bluff Meat Supply chain of butcheries. I have a demonstrated history in product management and placement as well as operations management.  I am a qualified addictions counselor and hope to make that my new career. I love to kitesurf and play drums piano and guitar, and I can talk about those subjects, Music, recovery, kiting for hours. I aim to be a professional counselor, and live a peaceful fulfilled life.
in my Career, highlights that stand out are My Five MTN Radio Awards for the best news and actuality show and best business show on national radio. Also the honour of mixing the Artist Seal at Sun City Superbowl in 2006.

## parts *(object)* 

- Setting up a car wash requires careful planning and consideration of several key factors:

1. Location: Choose a visible and accessible location with high traffic flow.
2. Permits and regulations: Research and obtain the necessary permits and licenses required to operate a car wash in your area.
3. Business plan: Develop a comprehensive business plan outlining your services, target market, pricing strategy, and financial projections.
4. Equipment: Invest in high-quality car wash equipment such as pressure washers, vacuums, brushes, and water recycling systems.
5. Facilities: Build or lease a facility that includes bays for washing and vacuuming, as well as waiting areas for customers.
6. Staff: Hire and train employees to operate the car wash equipment and provide excellent customer service.
7. Marketing: Develop a marketing strategy to attract customers, including signage, online presence, and promotions.
8. Supplies: Purchase cleaning chemicals, towels, and other supplies needed for car washing.
9. Insurance: Obtain insurance coverage for your car wash business to protect against potential liabilities.
10. Maintenance: Regularly maintain and inspect equipment to ensure smooth operations and customer satisfaction.

By addressing these aspects, you'll be well on your way to setting up a successful car wash business. *(string)*

## parts *(object)* 

- When conducting a feasibility study for a car wash business, consider the following factors:

1. Market Analysis: Evaluate the demand for car wash services in your target area. Consider factors such as population density, vehicle ownership rates, and competition from existing car wash businesses.

2. Location: Assess potential locations for your car wash, considering factors such as visibility, accessibility, proximity to residential areas or commercial centers, and zoning regulations.

3. Customer Demographics: Understand the demographics of your target market, including their income levels, preferences, and expectations for car wash services.

4. Competition: Research existing car wash businesses in the area to understand their offerings, pricing, and market share. Identify opportunities to differentiate your car wash and attract customers.

5. Pricing Strategy: Determine the pricing for your car wash services based on the local market, the level of service offered, and your cost structure. Consider offering competitive pricing while maintaining profitability.

6. Equipment and Technology: Evaluate the cost and quality of car wash equipment, including automated systems, pressure washers, vacuums, and water recycling systems. Consider investing in technology that improves efficiency and enhances customer experience.

7. Operational Considerations: Estimate the operating costs of your car wash business, including labor, utilities, maintenance, and supplies. Develop a plan for managing day-to-day operations efficiently.

8. Regulatory Requirements: Research and understand the permits, licenses, and regulations governing car wash businesses in your area. Ensure compliance with environmental regulations related to water usage and waste disposal.

9. Financial Projections: Develop financial projections for your car wash business, including startup costs, revenue forecasts, and break-even analysis. Consider factors such as pricing, customer volume, and seasonal variations in demand.

10. Risk Assessment: Identify potential risks and challenges that may impact the success of your car wash business, such as economic downturns, changes in consumer behavior, or unforeseen regulatory changes. Develop contingency plans to mitigate these risks.

By thoroughly evaluating these factors, you can determine the feasibility of starting a car wash business and make informed decisions to maximize your chances of success. *(string)*

**about_user_message** *(string)* : I'm 48 years old from Durban South Africa. I have been a sound engineer and producer for 25 years with a demonstrated history in broadcast technical production and sound engineering with top players in the media and broadcast industry, in addition to online video production, and content/copywriting for my own Company SoundsLucrative/Abundant Web. I also started a successful company that sells value added meat products to the food service and FMCG market called Rib Rage, where I was the Regional Operations Manager and Shareholder. I managed all accounts on the KZN North Coast and was instrumental in securing accounts with the Spar group as well as the Bluff Meat Supply chain of butcheries. I have a demonstrated history in product management and placement as well as operations management.  I am a qualified addictions counselor and hope to make that my new career. I love to kitesurf and play drums piano and guitar, and I can talk about those subjects, Music, recovery, kiting for hours. I aim to be a professional counselor, and live a peaceful fulfilled life.
in my Career, highlights that stand out are My Five MTN Radio Awards for the best news and actuality show and best business show on national radio. Also the honour of mixing the Artist Seal at Sun City Superbowl in 2006.

Dear Dolphin Coast Radio,

I trust this message finds you well. We appreciate the opportunity to collaborate on the production of your radio advert for Competitive Carports (CCP-45-001-E).

Below is the detailed breakdown of the services provided:

1. Script Writing: R100.00
2. Voiceover: R150.00
3. Recording: R100.00
4. Production: R150.00

Total: R500.00

Please find attached the official invoice for your records. We kindly request payment within the stipulated terms.

If you have any queries or require further clarification, feel free to reach out.

Best regards,

Robert [Last Name]
Sounds Lucrative
